questions.a: THE NARROWING IS NOT THE KILLED TOLERANCE, BY THAT RULE'S OWN TEST. The prior ticket's general shape is 'a tolerance is a forger's costume whenever the forger can produce the thing being tolerated.' It killed a tolerance of an unlinked leading PREFIX — and a forger can produce an unlinked prefix, since a total overwrite is one, which is why it fell. What is tolerated here is unlinked entries sitting BENEATH a newest link that verifies, and the forger cannot produce the required half: a link that hashes the current prefix comes only from the store's own _link_for, at which point calling the door is cheaper than forging. The rule and this narrowing agree.

THE DIAGNOSTIC IS NOT THE GATE, AND BOTH ARE KEPT. inspect_trail retains all three lanes and keeps checking the whole trail — it localizes a tamper to its earliest entry, which is what a census tooth should print and what complete-diagnostic-on-first-pass wants. Only standing()'s GATING question narrows. The instrument stays as sharp as it is; the gate stops answering a wider question than it was asked.

THE OLD-ENTRY-TAMPER CASE IS COVERED BY THE MERKLE PROPERTY, NOT BY THE TRAIL WALK. test_an_EDIT_to_an_older_entry_breaks_the_newest_link asserts breaks on entry 0 AND entry 1 — entry 1 being the newest — so the top link already catches it. The tooth's docstring claims the tamper is 'invisible to a newest entry reader'; that describes a reader of the newest RECORD's content, which is not what standing() will do.

WHAT WHOLE-TRAIL GATING ACTUALLY BOUGHT, stated so the loss is deliberate: localization of the earliest tamper point (kept — it moves to inspect_trail and the census tooth), and refusal on unlinked OLD entries (dropped on purpose — that is the class Akien ruled irrelevant once the point the evidence centred on is resolved).

THE QUARANTINE DESIGN IS WITHDRAWN AND WHY IT WAS WRONG BEYOND BEING UNNECESSARY. It would have written a ruling-shaped record into the trail permanently — a thing existing only because Akien signed it — at the moment the standing aim is to remove him from the process. 'I HAVE TO BE PART OF THE PROCESS. And we're trying slowly to remove me from the process' (Akien, 2026-08-16). The repointed gate needs no ruling at all, and that is a property of the fix worth naming, not a side effect.

standing()'s PRINTED REMEDY IS FALSE FOR THIS CLASS. It says 'Recover the trail from git and re-run the proof'; measured across every commit of test_host.json, entry 1 arrived unlinked at its first commit and carries no link at any commit. The sentence was written for the destroy-the-history attack and inherited by the never-came-through-the-door case. It is corrected as part of this ticket.

workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(the-door-is-the-only-path-in-practice) -> PROVED -> [SUPERSEDED]

watchme.trigger: every pulse reaching the tester's shim — the probe globs every **/validations/*.json in class-space (files only: no device, no bus, no network), counts entries dated after this fix lands, and fires when >= 20 such entries exist AND one or more carries no trail_link
watchme.enough: cleared when >= 20 post-fix entries exist AND every one carries a link. The floor sits on BOTH clauses deliberately: a clear with no sample floor retires before it can fire, the asymmetry that made does_optional_mean_never_carried clear at n=1 on its own first pulse.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier, carrying the count of post-fix entries, the count and addresses of any unlinked ones, and the callers that wrote them
watchme.consumer: cairn/devices/tester — the self-route the tester's charter already records, because persist_validation is the hand that mints a link and it lives at that address

intent_berth: none, because this ticket entered at TICKET, not at INTENT — ruling 2026-08-02-three-entry-points-and-structural-refiled: a bug goes straight to TICKET. Its thinking artifact is the trouble record named in from_trouble, which carries the defect, the measurement and the fix-when-taken.

proof: cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_validation_store.py — 16 teeth (roster floor raised 11 -> 16), including the four the falsifier names: an unlinked OLD entry under a verifying newest link still stands; a FORGED newest entry cannot borrow a link (no link, and a link copied from entry 0); an edit to an OLDER entry still refuses at standing() (the over-narrowing guard); and the corpus census — every one of the 90 real validation trails in class-space has a newest entry whose link verifies, asserted as an invariant over a population floor of 70 rather than the snapshot 90, and red on both vacuous cases (a known-bad fixture corpus, and an empty glob). cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_tester.py — 8 teeth, roster floor now DERIVED from the module's own '^def test_' declarations rather than typed, including test_run_proof_REQUIRES_a_sink_and_has_no_default_for_it. Both run bare, twice, exit 0, and both are sealed green under the tester at isolation='netns' (seal verdict 'sealed': 1.1.1.1:53 reachable bare, unreachable inside netns). AGAINST THE OLD CODE (Law 8): three teeth observed FAILING against HEAD's validation_store.py and device.py loaded under importlib — the git stash the plan named was unsafe against 24 unrelated modified files, so `git show HEAD:` was used instead, which is the stronger instrument. The other two teeth pass both ways BY DESIGN; they guard against over-narrowing rather than witness the change, and counting them as five would have been the hollow reading.
